questions.prompt: Why does the listener not retry the request at once, as it does for a rate limit?
options: The provider forbids a second request
The same request fails the same way, so something must become smaller first
A retry would delete the record
The loop cannot run a step twice
questions.explanation: A too-large request does not pass with time. Only a smaller surface can change the result, so the listener shortens it first.

questions.prompt: No safe range exists, so no summary lands and replaceCount stays the same. What does the listener do?
options: It calls next(), so the turn ends with the error
It waits and retries with backoff
questions.explanation: The listener retries only when replaceCount rose. Without a change, a retry would fail the same way, so it passes the error on.

questions.prompt: Why does the recovery select a range with 0 tokens to keep, not the usual 1,440?
options: Zero makes the summary request free
The provider requires an empty history
The request is already over the limit, so it must shrink as much as is safe
Zero keeps the system prompt out of the range
questions.explanation: The provider already said the request is too large. Keeping 0 tokens shortens as much as a safe cut allows, while the newest call and result stay together.
